evidence_scope: AI-assisted development tasks documented from actual debugging, enhancement, and business-mapping work on this project.
principle: AI proposes; the human owner reviews, tests, and owns the final decision.

records.title: Dependency failure diagnosis and durable fix
records.problem: The pipeline completed its analytics steps but failed while generating a Markdown report because pandas.DataFrame.to_markdown() requires the optional tabulate package.
records.prompt_excerpt: The pipeline fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tabulate'. Diagnose the root cause and provide a durable fix, not only a one-time workaround.
ai_contribution: Recommended installing tabulate and adding it to requirements.txt.
Recommended rerunning the entire pipeline rather than checking only the failing line.
human_decisions: Confirmed the traceback location before applying the recommendation.
Added tabulate as an explicit project dependency.
Kept report generation unchanged because the issue was dependency management, not business logic.
verification: Installed the dependency in the project virtual environment.
Reran the complete pipeline successfully.
Opened the Streamlit dashboard and confirmed that reports and tabs loaded.
records.impact: Restored the full reporting workflow and made future installations reproducible.

records.title: Auditable AI-development evidence and enablement design
records.problem: The project demonstrated analytics skills, but the use of AI during development was not visible, auditable, or reusable by another team member.
records.prompt_excerpt: Show evidence of AI-assisted development in the project in the most impressive but truthful way.
ai_contribution: Proposed a dedicated dashboard tab for transparent AI-use evidence.
Structured each record around problem, prompt, AI contribution, human decision, verification, and impact.
Created reusable prompt templates and a lightweight AI-adoption playbook.
human_decisions: Kept the evidence local and deterministic so the demo does not depend on an external AI API.
Excluded unsupported claims, confidential data, credentials, and invented time-savings.
Required human verification and artifact references for every documented AI contribution.
verification: Validated the JSON evidence schema.
Added automated tests for the evidence assets.
Compiled the dashboard code and reran the full test suite.
records.impact: Makes AI usage transparent, interview-ready, and reusable for team onboarding and upskilling.

records.title: GTM transferability mapping
records.problem: The demonstration dataset is financial, so the business relevance to Sales Operations and GTM decision support needed to be explained without pretending to use company data.
records.prompt_excerpt: Map this reusable time-series pipeline to GTM Operations while clearly separating the demonstration data from a real company dataset.
ai_contribution: Mapped stock symbols to regions, accounts, products, or sales teams.
Mapped returns and volatility to KPI movement, variability, and unusual changes.
Suggested a stakeholder-focused narrative around regional monitoring, anomaly detection, and repeatable SQL reporting.
human_decisions: Marked the mapping as conceptual and did not imply access to Red Hat or customer data.
Kept the analytical architecture reusable while preserving the financial demonstration dataset.
Selected examples that align with Business Analyst and GTM Operations responsibilities.
verification: Reviewed each mapping for analytical equivalence.
Added a clear transferability statement to the Executive Overview.
Added a GTM adoption blueprint to the AI evidence tab.
records.impact: Connects the technical workflow to regional business decisions, stakeholder reporting, and operational efficiency.

records.title: Cursor project rules and repository-aware review workflow
records.problem: Repository-aware AI assistance can accelerate Python and SQL work, but team adoption needs persistent guardrails for privacy, analytical correctness, Snowflake safety, testing, and scope control.
records.prompt_excerpt: Review @src/gtm_demo.py, @src/snowflake_adapter.py, and @sql/snowflake_gtm_analysis.sql. Explain the data flow, propose the smallest low-risk improvement, and provide verification steps. Follow @Cursor Rules and do not change files until the plan is approved.
ai_contribution: Uses explicit repository file context instead of isolated copy-pasted snippets.
Applies version-controlled Cursor project rules to every relevant Agent or Inline Edit request.
Creates a repeatable plan-review-diff-test-document workflow for analyst enablement.
human_decisions: Restricted all GTM examples to synthetic data and prohibited claims of company-data access.
Required plan approval before edits and line-by-line diff review afterward.
Kept execution, credential use, destructive SQL, and final analytical decisions under human control.
verification: Added .cursor/rules/analytics-quality.mdc as a version-controlled project rule.
Added AGENTS.md and docs/CURSOR_WORKFLOW.md with completion checks and a safe demo prompt.
Added tests that verify the rule exists and contains privacy, Snowflake, and testing guardrails.
records.impact: Demonstrates how Cursor can be adopted as a governed team capability rather than an unstructured individual coding shortcut.

records.title: Snowflake-ready GTM analytics and safe live-connection adapter
records.problem: The project needed to demonstrate cloud data-warehouse knowledge and direct GTM relevance without depending on company credentials or pretending to use real sales data.
records.prompt_excerpt: Add a Snowflake-ready integration and a synthetic GTM decision-support demo. Keep the default demo fully local, never store credentials, require explicit confirmation before writes, and clearly separate live readiness from a verified live connection.
ai_contribution: Structured an optional Snowflake adapter using environment-based configuration and safe readiness checks.
Proposed Snowflake-native SQL examples using CTEs, window functions, QUALIFY, COUNT_IF, and DIV0.
Mapped a deterministic synthetic GTM dataset to regional pipeline, bookings, win rate, activity, and explainable review events.
human_decisions: Kept Snowflake optional so the interview demo remains stable without external services.
Disabled live actions unless the connector, required fields, authentication, and explicit upload confirmation are present.
Used only synthetic demonstration data and displayed no secrets or account identifiers.
verification: Generated and validated deterministic synthetic GTM output.
Compiled the Snowflake adapter without requiring credentials.
Tested identifier validation, read-only query restrictions, SQL assets, and no-secret readiness output.
Ran the full pipeline, test suite, and Streamlit application test.
records.impact: Connects the portfolio project directly to GTM Operations and demonstrates a production-aware path from Python analytics to governed Snowflake reporting.

records.title: Interview-grade decision intelligence redesign and project-wide preflight
records.problem: The project contained strong individual features, but the eight tabs needed one coherent stakeholder story, clearer GTM relevance, stronger reliability evidence, and a safer interview launch workflow.
records.prompt_excerpt: Improve every tab and the complete project so it is extraordinary and impressive for the Business Analyst AI-adoption interview, while keeping claims truthful and the demo stable.
ai_contribution: Proposed a project-wide information architecture covering executive decisions, driver analysis, explainable investigation, SQL and Snowflake, reliability, operational transferability, AI assurance, and team adoption.
Structured deterministic decision briefs, human-context questions, read-only SQL safeguards, a 30-60-90 adoption plan, skill-gap mapping, and interview-focused documentation.
Created a repeatable Windows preflight workflow that runs the pipeline, tests, data-quality checks, and artifact checks before Streamlit starts.
human_decisions: Kept public market data as the core analytical demonstration and labelled all GTM and operational records as synthetic.
Rejected unsupported claims of Red Hat data access, live Snowflake use, or measured productivity gains.
Prioritized a stable seven-minute interview route instead of demonstrating every feature.
Retained human ownership of analytical interpretation, SQL execution, accepted changes, and stakeholder recommendations.
verification: Compiled all core Python modules successfully.
Ran the complete pipeline and regenerated all analytical outputs.
Passed the complete automated test suite.
Generated a PASS preflight summary with a 100/100 data-quality score.
Executed all dashboard data paths through a local no-network test harness.
records.impact: Transforms the portfolio into a coherent, reproducible, role-specific demonstration of decision intelligence and governed team AI adoption.

prompt_library.name: Debug with evidence
prompt_library.prompt: Analyze this traceback. Identify the root cause, distinguish it from downstream symptoms, propose the smallest durable fix, and give me a verification checklist. Do not rewrite unrelated code.

prompt_library.name: Review an analytics feature
prompt_library.prompt: Review this analytics function for correctness, edge cases, data leakage, and readability. Explain every recommended change. I will decide which changes to accept and will test them independently.

prompt_library.name: Translate analysis for stakeholders
prompt_library.prompt: Convert these validated analytical findings into a concise stakeholder summary. Separate observed facts, interpretation, risks, and recommended next actions. Do not invent missing context or causal claims.

prompt_library.name: Create an onboarding use case
prompt_library.prompt: Turn this completed AI-assisted task into a reusable onboarding guide with the business goal, approved inputs, prompt template, human checks, expected output, limitations, and escalation conditions.

prompt_library.name: Review Snowflake SQL in Cursor
prompt_library.prompt: Review @sql/snowflake_gtm_analysis.sql with @Cursor Rules. Check Snowflake syntax, window partitions, analytical assumptions, data-privacy boundaries, and query cost. Propose the smallest patch and a read-only verification plan. Do not execute SQL or expose credentials.

prompt_library.name: Investigate a GTM KPI change
prompt_library.prompt: Using only the supplied validated synthetic KPI extract, identify the largest material changes. Separate observed facts, possible interpretations, uncertainty, and analyst follow-up questions. Do not infer causality or invent business context.

responsible_use: Treat AI output as a proposal, not a final answer.
Verify code by running tests and reviewing changed lines.
Verify analytical claims against source data and calculations.
Document accepted, rejected, and modified suggestions.
Escalate security, legal, privacy, or domain-critical uncertainty.
